subject: Accounting
title: Zero-Based Budgeting
description: A fast breakdown of Zero-Based Budgeting for builders.

hook.text: Most budgets start with last year's numbers. Zero-based budgeting starts from scratch—every time.

buildup.text: Every expense must be justified from zero. No department gets funding just because it did last year.

discovery.text: This forces managers to rethink priorities and eliminate spending that no longer adds value.

twist.text: It's thorough but exhausting—many organizations try it once and go back to traditional methods.

climax.text: When done well, zero-based budgeting can find millions in savings hidden by routine spending.

punchline.text: Start from zero. Justify every dollar. Keep only what matters.

quiz.question: How does zero-based budgeting differ from traditional budgeting?
options: Every expense must be justified from zero each period

details.summary: Zero-based budgeting requires every expense to be justified from scratch each period, rather than using last year's budget as a starting point. This topic explains the ZBB process, its advantages in eliminating waste, and the significant time investment it requires.
details.whyItMatters: Traditional budgeting perpetuates past spending patterns, including waste. Zero-based budgeting forces every dollar to prove its value, making it a powerful tool for organizations serious about cost discipline.
takeaways: ZBB starts from zero—every activity must be justified as if the budget were being created for the first time
It surfaces spending that continues only because of inertia, not because it adds value
The trade-off is significant: ZBB requires vastly more time and effort than incremental budgeting

faq.question: What is zero-based budgeting?
faq.answer: Zero-based budgeting is a method where every expense must be justified for each new budget period starting from a base of zero. Unlike traditional budgeting that adjusts last year's numbers, ZBB requires managers to build their budget from scratch and defend every dollar.

faq.question: What are the disadvantages of zero-based budgeting?
faq.answer: ZBB is extremely time-consuming, requiring detailed analysis and justification for every activity every period. It can also lead to short-term thinking if essential long-term investments are cut because their immediate value is hard to quantify.
